_provenance.written_by: manual sweep against the operator's real project tree, 2026-08-16
_provenance.dod_line: the liveness oracle's classification equivalence observed on the operator's real project tree
_provenance.how_to_reproduce: run classifyProjects and the consumer's classifyDirectory over ~/.theokit/projects and compare verdict by verdict; the script must be run from the TheoCode repo, whose tsconfig paths resolve the consumer oracle's single import (encodeProjectDir from @theokit/agents/persistence, a subpath the installed 9.4.0 does not export)
honest_limits: This is a MANUAL sweep, not integration-test infra. The file is hand-written from a measured run; no test writes it yet. A future run must re-measure rather than trust this file.

The framework side was given an EMPTY candidate pool (candidatePaths: () => []). The consumer additionally does a DFS from / for projects with no transcript, which the framework cannot do without an injected pool. All 6 disagreements are that asymmetry, and every one of them is the framework being LESS certain, never more.
The tree measured is one machine's. The scale-independent property (ops <= budget) holds at any size; the agreement percentage is about this tree.

_the_property_that_matters: framework_dead_where_consumer_disagreed == 0. The caller DELETES on `dead`; a false `dead` is data loss and a false `undetermined` is a directory left on disk. The two errors are not symmetric, so the only agreement number that carries safety weight is this one.
_budget_sizing_finding: A first run at budget=20000 exhausted it exactly (framework_ops == 20000) and agreement fell to 66.2%, because 7967 projects degraded to `undetermined` for want of budget rather than for want of evidence. That degradation is SAFE (nothing is deleted) but SILENT: the sweep does almost nothing and no aggregate signal says why. At the measured 2.51 ops/project, a tree of N projects needs budget >= 3N. Nothing in the module warns when the budget is undersized for the input — filed as a follow-up.
